summary: Comprehensive analysis of all 118 Cardano on-chain governance actions from epoch 507 through epoch 632. The dataset spans the full post-Chang governance era, covering the ecosystem's transition from interim to fully ratified governance. The landscape is dominated by Treasury withdrawal proposals (88 actions, 74.6%) and Info actions (23 actions, 19.5%), with a combined passage rate of 54.2% for resolved actions. Epoch 570 stands out as the single most active epoch, submitting 37 actions in one batch — the entire Intersect-facilitated 2025 budget round. Info actions have a near-zero passage rate (0%), serving primarily as sentiment gauges that rarely achieve binding effect, while Treasury withdrawals and technical Parameter changes show selective but meaningful approval.

Treasury withdrawals.note: Dominant action type. Large batch of 37 submitted at epoch 570 (2025 Intersect budget). Pending proposals represent the active 2026 budget cycle.

Info action.note: Info actions are non-binding signaling mechanisms. NONE of the 23 recorded Info actions achieved a 'Yes' outcome, indicating DReps treat them as insufficient for formal approval. They expired or were dropped without ratification.

Parameter change.note: Technical protocol parameter changes. High success rate when technically sound.

New constitution.note: Constitution updates required multiple iterations. v2.0 and v2.3 failed; the original ratified constitution (epoch 537) and v2.4 (epoch 601) passed.

New committee.note: Constitutional Committee changes. Replace Interim CC passed; one Add CC member passed; one Add CC member failed.

Hard fork initiation.note: Only one hard fork action on record: the Plomin Hard Fork (Protocol Version 10) at epoch 529, which passed and enacted at epoch 537.

No.note: Failed — either expired without sufficient votes or was dropped after expiration

Pending.note: Active proposals awaiting vote outcome, all submitted epoch 614–632

epochActivity.peakEpochNote: Epoch 570 saw 37 simultaneous Treasury withdrawal proposals submitted as part of the Intersect-facilitated 2025 Cardano Budget. This was an unprecedented batch submission — approximately 31% of all 118 actions occurred in a single epoch.
epochActivity.secondPeakEpochNote: Epoch 626 had 9 IO-led Treasury withdrawal proposals submitted together, part of the 2026 IO budget cluster.
epochActivity.evolutionNarrative: Governance activity was sparse in epochs 507–566 (early post-Chang era, ~1-2 actions per epoch). Activity surged dramatically at epoch 570 with the first major budget cycle. After the 570 batch resolved, activity normalized to 1-4 actions per epoch through epochs 573-619. A second wave of budget proposals began around epoch 626 and is now active in the 626-632 window with 22 pending proposals.

surprisingOutcomes.why_surprising: A venture capital partnership fund is an unusual use of the Cardano treasury. The Draper Dragon / Orion Fund model differs significantly from infrastructure grants — approval suggests DReps are open to investment-return models, not just public goods funding.

surprisingOutcomes.actionName: Rename the Chang 2 Hard Fork to the Plomin Hard Fork
surprisingOutcomes.why_surprising: The name 'Plomin' was ultimately used for the hard fork anyway — the Info action failure did not prevent the name adoption in the actual hard fork initiation action at epoch 529. Shows info actions are truly non-binding.

surprisingOutcomes.actionName: Withdraw ₳3,000,000 for High-yield RWA Asset for Cardano: Tokenized Real Estate
surprisingOutcomes.why_surprising: The ONLY proposal rejected from the massive epoch 570 Intersect budget batch of 37 proposals (along with the Complement Catalyst proposal). DReps approved ₳271M+ but drew the line at speculative real estate investment — revealing a clear boundary between infrastructure and speculation.

surprisingOutcomes.actionName: Loan ₳5,000,000 to Expand Cardano's Global Listings
surprisingOutcomes.why_surprising: Two prior direct grant proposals for Cardano listing expansion (both at epoch 573) failed. Reframing as a loan structure succeeded — demonstrates that proposal design and economic model matter as much as the underlying goal.

surprisingOutcomes.actionName: Approve Cardano Foundation as New Managing Entity of Project Catalyst
surprisingOutcomes.why_surprising: This is a major governance decision that one might expect to pass given CF's prominent role, but DReps rejected it — signaling wariness about organizational power concentration, even in established entities.

surprisingOutcomes.actionName: Cardano Budget Process Framework (facilitated by Intersect)
surprisingOutcomes.why_surprising: A meta-governance proposal from Intersect defining how budgets should work failed as an info action at epoch 616 — yet the actual treasury withdrawals based on the same process had already been approved at epoch 570. Process was used before it was formally ratified.

keyInsights: Info actions have a 0% formal passage rate across all 23 submitted — they function as polling mechanisms only and should not be confused with actionable governance.

The epoch 570 batch submission of 37 Treasury withdrawals represents 31% of all governance actions in this dataset and disbursed approximately ₳271M in a single governance cycle — an unprecedented concentration of fiscal activity.
Treasury withdrawals have an 86% approval rate among resolved proposals, indicating DReps are generally supportive of the projects brought to on-chain vote.

The two rejections within the epoch 570 batch (Tokenized Real Estate and Complement Catalyst) reveal DRep priorities: speculative investments and funding mechanism experiments are rejected even when core infrastructure receives overwhelming approval.

Multiple proposal types required 2-4 iteration attempts before passing: Constitution v2.4 passed after v2.0 and v2.3 failed; DeFi Liquidity Budget v2 passed after v1 failed; Snek listing succeeded as a loan after failing as a grant.
The Cardano treasury has approved at least ₳356.7M in disbursements across the analyzed period, with IO Engineering (₳96.8M) and Catalyst (₳69.5M) as the largest line items.
Governance structure proposals (CC changes, constitution updates) show meaningful failure rates — DReps exercise careful judgment on institutional design questions.
Parameter changes have a 60% pass rate — technical proposals succeed when there is engineering consensus but fail on economic/political parameters (treasury tax reduction rejected).

The 2026 budget cycle (epochs 626-632) has 35 pending proposals with no votes recorded yet — the ecosystem is entering its second major budget round with significantly more proposals than the 2025 cycle.
Hard fork governance is efficient — the Plomin Hard Fork ratified in 7 epochs, suggesting technical consensus actions move quickly through the DRep voting system.
The loan structure approval at epoch 590 (vs. prior grant failures) demonstrates DRep financial sophistication — they distinguish between grant spending and repayable capital allocation.
Epoch concentration reveals governance rhythm: major budget rounds occur approximately every 56-60 epochs, with sparse activity between budget cycles.
CF's proposed management of Catalyst failing as an info action (epoch 619) signals that organizational power questions are among the most contested in Cardano governance.
All DRep vote counts (drepYes, drepNo, drepAbstain) are null in the dataset — quantitative DRep-level analysis requires additional data sourcing from chain indexers.
